newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to join Paris Club this year - Yeltsin.
newsitem.headline: Russia to join Paris Club this year - Yeltsin.

text.p: Russia will join the Paris Club of creditor nations this year to facilitate repayment at better terms of about $37 billion of foreign debt owed to Moscow, President Boris Yeltsin said on Wednesday.
"This year Russia will join the Paris Club," Yeltsin said in a radio address. "It will help us get back the money owed to Russia by many countries of the world."
Referring to his summit last week in Helsinki with U.S. President Bill Clinton, Yeltsin alluded to plans for Russia to join the next Group of Seven (G7) meeting of leading industrial nations.
"The U.S. President promised me that at the next G-7 meeting Russia will enjoy the full rights of a member of the club of the most developed countries of the world," he said.
"The G-7 will be turned into the G-8. This summer in the U.S. at the next (G-7) meeting I shall have a chance to check how our partners keep their promise."
Representatives of the group will meet in Denver from June 20-22.
Russia became one of the world's biggest creditors, when it inherited the foreign assets of the former Soviet Union, including $132 billion in foreign debts the Soviet Union had extended.
Some of Russia's debtors, accounting for $37 billion of the debt, either have signed restructuring agreements with the Club or plan to do so.
The Club has favourable terms for creditors due in part to Club rules restricting debtors from offering better repayment terms to non-Club creditors.
Russia has been slow to join because it must agree to discount its assets to become a Club member.
